item.title: Kerry had above average rate of flu this winter
item.description: Kerry has had an above average rate of flu this winter season. Latest data from the Health Protection Surveillance Centre shows there have been 656 flu cases recorded in Kerry since the beginning of the winter season. 80 of those cases were in the week up to January 3rd. Advertisement The rate of flu per 100,000 population in Kerry this winter season is 419.3, well above the national average of 352.6. Kerry’s rate of flu last week was 51.1, again above the national average of 39.8.

item.title: Just one part-time dentist serving Kenmare following retirement of last full-time dentist
item.description: Kenmare could be demonstrative of a potential crisis facing dental practices across rural Ireland. The south Kerry town’s last full-time dentist retired at Christmas, and the sole remaining part-time dentist operates just three days a week. Recently, councillor Teddy O'Sullivan Casey contacted the HSE stressing the importance of attracting more dentists to Kenmare, and asking what role the executive would play in this. item.title: Minister of State denies Government’s decision to reject Mercosur deal is tokenism
item.description: Minister of State Michael Healy-Rae has denied that the Government’s decision to reject the Mercosur trade deal is tokenism or grandstanding, as it's likely to pass anyway. EU member states are to vote on the trade deal tomorrow; this deal would increase trade opportunities between Europe and Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay. item.title: One Pub, One Family, Five Generations, and a Farewell
item.description: Mike ‘Larkin’ McCarthy’s family has run Larkin’s pub in Milltown since the 1860s. Mike has retired. However, the much-loved pub and restaurant will continue under new hands. Mike reflects on a lifetime growing up and working in the business. Advertisement

item.title: Minister of State with responsibility for Further Education visits Kerry College campus
item.description: The Minister of State with responsibility for Further Education is visiting Kerry today. Independent Deputy for Sligo, Leitrim, North Roscommon and South Donegal, Marian Harkin is in the county on a number of engagements this afternoon. The Junior Minister is visiting Tralee, where she is attending Kerry College’s Monavalley campus. Advertisement Minister of State Harkin received a tour of the premises and will partake in a presentation at Kerry College this afternoon.

item.title: Over €9 million won by National Lottery players in Kerry in 2025
item.description: €9,301,955.20 has been won by National Lottery players in Kerry in 2025. Figures released by the National Lottery to Radio Kerry show there were eight high tier jackpots won in the county as of December 19th. The past 12 months saw one new millionaire in the county from National Lottery wins.
